claims.text: Cerium is the rare-earth additive selected for modifying the boride-based components.
Adding 1 wt% Ce to boride-based components will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion relative to untreated components.
The Ce-modified components will exhibit a 35% improvement in molten-aluminum corrosion resistance.
The predicted 35% improvement applies at 700°C after 100 hours of exposure to molten aluminum.
Adding Ce causes a protective oxide layer to form on the surface of the boride-based components.
The protective oxide layer hinders diffusion of aluminum ions into the material.
Hindering aluminum diffusion into the material improves resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
The intervention should remain effective between 600°C and 800°C.
The intervention should remain effective for molten-aluminum exposure times between 50 and 150 hours.
The magnitude of the corrosion-resistance improvement may depend on the specific composition of the boride-based component.
The magnitude of the corrosion-resistance improvement may depend on processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 35% improvement, but the experiment only falsifies it below 20%. An improvement from 20% to less than 35% would fail the stated quantitative prediction without meeting the stated falsification rule.
